question: What is the primary purpose of suture removal once a wound has healed sufficiently?

options.B: To prevent tissue reaction and infection caused by foreign material
options.C: To restart the primary inflammatory phase of wound healing
options.D: To stretch the scar tissue for better flexibility

explanation: Sutures are foreign materials that can cause tissue reactions, scarring, and infections if left in place longer than necessary after healing has occurred. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h1)

question: Which of the following must a nurse verify before proceeding with suture removal?

options.A: That the patient has paid all hospital bills
options.B: That a formal order from the healthcare provider is present and healing has occurred
options.C: That the patient has received a tetanus booster within the last week
options.D: That the wound is completely covered with a tight plaster

explanation: Nurses must ensure that primary intention healing has occurred and that there is a formal order from the healthcare provider before removing sutures. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h1)

question: Why are facial sutures typically removed earlier than sutures on the back or over joints?

options.A: Facial skin has poor blood supply which delays healing
options.B: Early removal prevents permanent suture track scarring in a high-visibility area
options.C: Facial muscles experience constant high tension
options.D: Facial sutures are made of dissolvable material only

explanation: Facial sutures are removed early (3 to 5 days) because the face has an abundant blood supply and early removal prevents unsightly ladder-track scarring. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h2)

question: What complication may occur if sutures are removed prematurely?
explanation: Removing sutures too early before the wound has gained sufficient tensile strength can lead to wound dehiscence, or re-opening of the incision. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h2)

question: Which of the following findings is a clear contraindication to suture removal?

options.B: Active purulent drainage and incomplete healing
options.C: Mild itching along the scar line
options.D: The passage of 7 days since surgery

explanation: Active purulent drainage and incomplete healing indicate infection and weakness, meaning sutures must remain in place and the surgeon notified. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h3)

question: Why is it important for a nurse to check for a history of anticoagulant use prior to suture removal?

options.A: It increases the risk of bleeding at the suture site
options.C: It speeds up epithelialization over the knots
options.D: It mandates the use of continuous sutures only

explanation: Anticoagulants impair blood clotting, which puts the patient at risk for bleeding when manipulating or cutting the skin around the sutures. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h3)

question: What is the correct technique when cleaning a suture line prior to removal?

options.A: Wipe from the outside edges inward toward the incision
options.B: Scrub vigorously with a dry gauze pad
options.C: Clean from the incision outward to prevent introducing contaminants
options.D: Pour hydrogen peroxide directly over the entire wound

explanation: Wiping from the clean incision outward prevents pushing microorganisms and debris from the surrounding skin back into the wound. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h4)

question: Which instrument is typically used to gently lift the suture knot away from the skin?
explanation: Sterile suture forceps are used to gently grasp and lift the knot, providing clearance for the tips of the suture scissors. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h4)

question: When removing an interrupted suture, why should the nurse cut only one side of the suture thread?

options.A: To leave a decorative pattern on the skin
options.B: So the contaminated surface portion does not get pulled through the deeper tissue
options.C: To keep the knot attached for future inspection
options.D: To prevent the scissors from becoming dull

explanation: Cutting one side allows the clean portion of the thread to be pulled out smoothly by the knot, avoiding dragging surface bacteria through the tissue channel. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h5)

question: What critical nursing action must be performed immediately after all sutures are removed?

options.A: Apply a tight compressive bandage over the whole limb
options.B: Count the removed sutures and compare with the documented number inserted
options.D: Administer a prophylactic dose of intravenous antibiotics

explanation: Counting the removed sutures against the documented record ensures that no broken fragments are left behind inside the wound. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h5)

question: What is the purpose of applying sterile adhesive strips (Steri-Strips) after suture removal?

options.A: To permanently seal the skin without scarring
options.B: To provide mechanical support and reduce tension across the wound edges
options.C: To deliver localized antibiotic medication continuously
options.D: To prevent the patient from seeing the scar

explanation: Adhesive strips help support the wound edges and reduce mechanical tension, lowering the risk of post-removal dehiscence or widening of the scar. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h6)

question: Which of the following instructions should a nurse give to a patient following suture removal?

options.A: Apply traditional herbal ointments to speed up skin softening
options.B: Keep the area clean and dry, and avoid picking at healing scabs
options.C: Scrub the incision vigorously with a sponge daily
options.D: Remove any supporting adhesive strips within two hours

explanation: Patients should be instructed to keep the incision clean and dry and to avoid picking at scabs to protect the delicate newly healed skin. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h6)

question: What complication can occur if a small piece of suture thread is accidentally left embedded beneath the skin?

options.B: Foreign body reaction, inflammation, or abscess formation
options.C: Immediate closure of the entire wound
options.D: Enhanced proliferation of healthy collagen fibers

explanation: Retained suture fragments act as foreign bodies that can trigger chronic inflammatory reactions, granulomas, or localized abscesses. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h7)

question: What immediate action should a nurse take if the wound edges begin to gape apart during suture removal?

options.A: Continue removing the remaining sutures quickly to finish the job
options.B: Stop the procedure, apply pressure, and notify the surgeon or healthcare provider
options.C: Apply an antiseptic ointment and send the patient home immediately
options.D: Ignore the gaping as it is a normal part of healing

explanation: Stopping the procedure prevents further damage; applying pressure and notifying the surgeon ensures the wound receives prompt re-evaluation and support. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h7)
